content.text:
The current dataset makes Splink worth evaluating, but it is mostly a name-matching problem with sparse identifier evidence.

- `FunderNameFeatures::from_name` derives every name column from one raw string. Normalized names, tokens, sorted tokens, cores, initials, aliases, and acronym expansions are correlated representations. Their agreement is not several independent confirmations. Explicit trading-as text supplies a relationship assertion within that same source string, rather than independent registry evidence. The docs' phrase “independent candidates” means separately available representations, not statistical independence. Source: [funder_name.rs](/Users/jamie/development/exposed-funder-resolution-20261007/exposed/src/lib/domain/models/funder_name.rs:60).
- The separate identity-bearing field is `donor_company_number`. `donor_kind` supplies a coarse source classification. Neither is verified externally. Only donors receive these fields; payer and ultimate-payer rows have null values by construction. Missing donor metadata on those roles is therefore structural missingness, not disagreement. There are no separate address, birth date, email, telephone, or registry-name fields in the funder table. Source: [declaration_cleaning.rs](/Users/jamie/development/exposed-funder-resolution-20261007/exposed/src/lib/domain/models/declaration_cleaning.rs:309), [Parquet schema](/Users/jamie/development/exposed-funder-resolution-20261007/exposed/src/lib/outbound/declaration_cleaning.rs:275).
- Member, declaration, register, role, source pointer, and payment references describe provenance and relationships. Sharing a payment or declaration does not establish the same funder: donor, intermediary payer, and ultimate payer can differ. Matching only within a member would also miss funders supporting several members. Amount, date, and category describe a funding event, not the funder's identity.
- A parent link and `IsUltimatePayerDifferent=false` support the proposed attribution rule. They do not establish donor identity or permit copying the donor's company number onto another role. Probabilistic identity linkage must remain separate from the attribution policy. Source: [resolution proposal](/Users/jamie/development/exposed-funder-resolution-20261007/docs/funder-resolution-design.md:35).
- Repeated payments deliberately create separate funder observations. Training on all observation pairs can disproportionately represent frequently repeated names and near-identical records. Evaluation can also leak if copies of a name or entity appear in both training and testing. Preserve occurrence IDs, but evaluate with grouped holdouts and examine results on unique evidence profiles as well as original observations. Source: [cleaning reference](/Users/jamie/development/exposed-funder-resolution-20261007/docs/declaration-cleaning.md:19).

My recommendation is an offline evaluation before any integration. Compare a restrained name-comparison model against exact normalized/core matching, using manually reviewed difficult pairs. Include different companies with similar names, person/organisation ambiguity, trading names, acronym collisions, and cross-role examples. Accepted company numbers can supply provisional labels, but mask the number when testing name-only performance. Source-reported identifiers are imperfect labels, and number-bearing donors may not represent unnamed payers.

The existing Parquet files provide a natural boundary for a Python/DuckDB experiment. Rust already owns extraction, typed source observations, publication, and proposed attribution. A separate experiment can read those files and return observation-pair scores plus model metadata without changing those contracts. Whether that experiment merits a production stage depends on its measured false merges and unresolved cases. No implementation, installation, or file changes were made.
